notes.title: Clockwork Ambrosia Development Update, Spring 2025
notes.notes:
Hey there everyone! I’m Lucy, our marketing manager here at OI Games. As of recently and looking forward, I’ll be the one keeping you updated about our projects at OI Games, including Clockwork Ambrosia! So let me catch you up to speed on Clockwork Ambrosia, share some big news for the future, and tell you a story about one of our early bosses, EIK0!

[previewyoutube=Szl4VPaBVdg;full][/previewyoutube]

First and foremost, we’re moving Clockwork Ambrosia’s release date. Although narrowing the game’s scope is important for creating a balanced player experience, the development team doesn’t want to compromise the overall experience. So they’re going to take a little bit more time, and our new target is November 2025.

But I am here to follow up that potentially sad news with potentially fun news! Development has recently completed our alpha phase, and we are now planning to start a public play test in the coming months! There will be plenty of enemies to tackle, bosses to battle, and weapon mods to mix and match to do the job! Plus I’ve got to say, get ready. I’ve been lucky enough to get my hands on internal testing versions, and it’s truly something special. I’ve put my reps in against EIK0 and I can’t wait to see how you all take her on!

If you aren’t already a subscriber to my new fantastic newsletter, head on over to https://oigames.substack.com and sign up so that you don’t miss out on future play test announcements!

Now on to the rest of our [strike]show[/strike] letter!

Boss Fight Origins: EIK0, The Baluster Engine
Originally EIK0 started off similar to the shield-wielding “Flat-iron” enemies that can be found around the Aqua Baluster, but our developers wanted something that was more than just a big enemy. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/e55a884e428252bfcd00dffe4cfc83249fbdb414.png

The Aqua Baluster is a massive piece of technology on the island, dredging up water from the sunken ruins below. To power all of this, the Baluster needed an engine, and that was where the team stumbled upon the idea of “what if the engine was the boss?” Separately from that, the idea of oozes infesting the tower was also on the mind, leading enemy developer, Ian Clark, to bring the two ideas together and create the first rendition we would recognize as EIK0.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/fa2b8a17a007ce2294f2e06227ced4ae768415f0.png

Ian moved forward with the idea of the ooze-infused engine, working with our artist, Maciej Kuczyński, to develop a look for our ooze-filled, corrupted machine. Adding ooze arms to a cinderblock was straightforward, but they needed to also work with the attack animations. Here’s the example he sent Maciej.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/202221d8cf2c7585af325bb6ebe8c08b995572bc.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/acb751712c4b5ad8a5e2a65e140676bed7136922.png

EIK0 really started to take shape and develop into the form you see today. Now the question was “how does an engine fight?”

From there Ian wanted to create a fun dynamic, something beyond a static sprite shooting lasers at you. The ooze inside is not intentionally fighting Iris, so how would it fight? With that mindset, all of EIK0’s attacks were themed around the idea of “thrashing around” in one form or another.

“Iris was just looking to figure out why the engine wasn’t working," Ian admitted. "Then she gets trapped in a room with an engine possessed by a raging bull.”

With that framework, the focus was on attacks that made sense but offer a frantic challenge that keeps you moving. By the nature of what they are, they aren’t targeted at Iris, so the attacks were designed to be “chaotic coincidences.” They were tempered down for more consistency, but that was the starting point.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/d423acaeec816861bea297bcc0b69109b400b23e.png

Now you may be wondering, what does EIK0 stand for? Well, it was actually originally named “ICK0”.

“It was a portmanteau of Ian’s name, and his home state of Oklahoma," Michael, Clockwork Ambrosia's producer, relates. This worked when I was the one implementing the boss. But when I stepped away from development, it became Ian’s baby, and I think it made him uncomfortable to have it named after him so directly.”

After that, the name shifted to EIK0, a pet name from the engineer who created the engine based on the existing model number in-universe.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35742780/47a5e4f797e61e7f2ab3378f3c11f46f9151633e.png

That’s all this time, but you can look forward to more Clockwork Ambrosia peeks as we approach the playtest beta and launch. Keep an eye out for further updates from the newsletter so you’re notified as soon as playtesting begins: https://oigames.substack.com 

‘Til next time!

- Lucy

Selection functionality is now more intuitive.
Swapping party members, selecting party members in menus, and scrolling through quest logs now behave more consistently in terms of left/right buttons. If you customized your keybindings, you may want to double-check your settings to avoid confusion with the new functionality.

New Save UI
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/66d38a8adf317463a90eb5f4696dec67a38562c1.png
New look and syntax for save files.
The save menu has a new look, which prevents the muddled text from appearing once players got to higher numbers of save slots. In general, it's easier to read, and the save file naming convention makes it more clear which campaign you're in and where.

Tali

notes.title: Tower Song v1.0 Complete Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Complete Patch Notes
Read on for a full list of changes made in this patch, both big and small!

New Features
New Player Character: Ezoan the Technomancer
 Play through the game as the Technomancer, Ezoan.
 Ezoan has been updated since the Prologue preview; his kit is now more "build and spend", focused on generating gravity through spells to deliver high value exosuit moves. 

New Dungeon: Lharif's Doom
 Obtain a new side quest in Qadam during Chapter 5
 Complete the new dungeon to obtain new legendary items
 Defeat a challenging new boss - or unlock its true secret

Character Reworks
 Akeno generates SP with his Blade of Elements and now spends SP to cast higher value spells.
 Kiran has been totally reworked; he now starts battle with zero MP and must build into his skills. He has new Damage-based abilities to compliment his Magic, and his Magic spells are generally more accessible. Most of his abilities have been tuned (details below), and he has several all-new abilities.
 Neat's finishers now gain extra effects with higher combos.
 Porphry is undergoing a significant rework still - look forward to our first major patch in the near future!
 Solace's Mana Battery and Overwatch have been reworked to allow Solace to gain and provide more direct benefit while using them.
 Tali can now give Jiji access to a new attack move.
 The Legionnaires Fred and Hudson now begin Chapter 6 with a new skill

Combat Enhancements
 New Enemy: Runner Queen - A terror in the desert who leads her swarm to eviscerate prey.
 New Enemy: Busaiya - A new look for the potted ephemera in the Fire Tower.
 Dodge (previously Evasion) and Regen are now stacking states like Wound.
 Enemy Types: All enemies are assigned a type, which grants them Defense bonuses and other resistances. These are viewable in battle. Enemies don't otherwise resist or absorb damage behind the scenes, unless buffed/debuffed during combat.

Campaign Enhancements
 There are more battles to conquer, items to craft, and loot to find!
 The world has come to life with more animation, characters, wildlife and unique character art for villagers
 The Guhar overworld map has been greatly improved, visually
 Most Fire Tower stages have been revisited with updated appearances and layouts
 The camera perspective has been adjusted for dungeons and other key moments to enhance the mood
 Flavor text has been added to objects throughout the game

Performance Enhancements
 We have added support for more international keyboards, such as French
 Map and combat performance has been improved across the game for all platforms.
 Steam Deck users can select the Performance Graphics preset to enjoy 60 FPS throughout the game (with some exceptions during scene loads or combat turns).
 Uers can also select a Minimal Graphics preset to achieve better performance on lower spec systems.

Warning: The below details may contain minor plot spoilers.

Achievements
 'So Much Damage' Achievement now requires 500 damage instead of 150
 Achievements unrelated to the main quest and storyline are no longer hidden in the Steam client.

Characters
Akeno
 New cut-scene portrait!
 Blades and Katanas grant the same damage bonus, but Katana now grants MP
 Blade of Elements skills generate SP.
 Cutting Wind, Mudquake, Soothe, Hard Water: Generate SP on use.
 Fire Spirit: Now grants Akeno Regen +2.
 Gale Force, Stonewall, Mudwall: MP no longer required to cast. SP required to cast.
 Phoenix Fire, Tsunami: MP no longer required to cast. SP required to cast.
 Phoenix Song: MP no longer required to cast. SP required to cast.
 Soothe: Bonus spirit now grants Regen +2.

Hudson
 Live Loadout: Remove cooldown; while switching weapons, players now see the current ammo count.

Fred
 Scythe no longer grants HP regen but instead a static HP bonus

Jiji
 New Ability - Lunar Strike: A single-target ability that deals bonus damage.
 Ward is now free, but has a 1-turn cooldown. It is no longer automatically cast on Tali.

Kiran
 New Ability - Determination: Passive talent that grants Kiran a Defense bonus based on his missing health.
 New Ability - Eldritch Strike: Deal critical Slashing Damage to target.
 New Ability - Indomitable: Once per battle, fully restore Kiran's MP and HP.
 New Ability - Knight Run: Cleanse party and grant immunity to negative states for 3 turns.
 New Ability - Soulblade: A powerful strike fueled by mana.
 Weapon damages re-balanced; generally, this means Broadswords have a higher Magic bonus than before, while Soulswords have bother high Damage and Magic bonuses than before.
 Bastion: Now grants MP when used.
 Dying Light: Now only deals damage based on Kiran's missing HP; damage overall decreased. MP cost cost decreased to compensate.
 Edification: Now triggers at a lower MP threshold.
 Eldritch Blast: Removed.
 Foothold: Now a passive talent that grants Kiran +30 MP on his first turn.
 Heroic Sacrifice: Now a free action that grants 50% MP for 50% HP.
 Honored Sacrifice: Removed.
 Mana Storm: Now strikes all targets; damage scales with Magic; MP cost scales with number of enemies.
 Mana Strike: Now a purely Magic skill.
 Matyr: Now a free action.
 Quantum Soul: MP restoration bonus reduced to 10.
 Siphon Strike: Damage reduced; MP gain increased.
 Soulchained Shock: MP cost reduced
 Spell Breaker: MP cost reduced
 Steel Hurricane: Now costs MP.

Neat
 No longer sees invalid moves in his skill list during combat.
 Crack now also stuns if Neat has Dodge
 Five Point Palm: Now a combo 4-5 finisher that inflicts Exploding Heart; after 3 turns, the target suffers 30% HP damage.
 Footwork: Now grants Dodge +3.
 Humble Warrior: Now grants Dodge +5.
 Knockout: No longer does bonus damage but inflicts Stun. At Combo 4+, it is a critical hit.
 Naudillon Shuffle: Now grants Dodge +3.
 Proud Warrior: Now grants Regen +3.
 Sigil: Now usable with any combo, but only grants Dodge (+5) at combo 4-5.
 Step In: Now grants Dodge +2.
 Unbreakable Combo: Now only grants 5% Damage bonus per Stage, and only starting at Stage 2
 Uppercut: No longer inflicts Stun but grants Neat a stack of Dodge per Combo. At Combo 4+, it is a free action.
 Water Bend: Now hits every enemy once but no longer wounds. At combo 4-5, it deals double damage.

Porphry
 Axe and Harbinger damage increased
 New Talent - Blood Sisters: Porphry can inflict up to Wound +8 to targets, rather than only Wound +5
 New Skill - Cauterize: Deal bonus damage to wounded targets.

 Carapace Slam: Now a tier 4 ability.

Solace
 Hit points increased

Tali
 Staves now grant HP instead of MP; wands now come with an MP penalty

Prologue

Soul Tower

Vistham

Fire Tower

Prologue

Quest

notes.title: Tower Song Content Update #1: The Fury
notes.notes:
Greetings Tower runners; welcome to the first Early Access content patch for Tower Song! This update includes our first new player character, Porphry the Fury! Plus, better controller support, totally revamped accessories and loot, and much, much more! Read on for details - and don't forget to leave us a review with your honest opinion! It means the world to us!

As always, a big thank you to our fans and players for your diligence in finding and reporting these problems to our development team! Props to the following bug hunters this go round:
Tortalius
Vorticia
Want to leave us feedback for this patch or the game in general? Head on over to feedback or find us on our Discord! 

If you don't want to miss future Tower Song updates, just joining our mailing list: https://oigames.substack.com

Major Changes 

New Player Character: Porphry the Fury
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/be2b83e904ff61e62251482ac45e3e21c750d322.png
Players can now complete the campaign as the Fury, Porphry.
Porphry is a true terror on the battlefield, and her campaign release comes with a completely reworked skillset from the original preview dungeon. Porphry engages in battle with her Battle Trance, a gauge that measures her dedication to the task at hand. Build her Trance to unlock truly devastating skills, but beware! If Porphry's Trance ever hits the threshold, she will temporarily loose control and go into a Berserker Rage, attacking a random target for many turns until the target - or Porphry - falls!

New Exploration Abilities
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/7739b2731d47df8e9c4610b09ecdc0c1be96106d.png
Each player character can access new areas with unique abilities.
Squeeze into caves with Jiji, smash through barriers with Porphry, or talk down Song-addled victims with Neat! Players can access unique, secret areas with their player character and find loot - and fight bosses! - not reachable with other characters.

Loot Revamp
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/d2598bd876981dbaa95050bae706252e31ca8b7c.png
Many more treasures to find, and many equipments overhauled.
We all love loot! Players can now find many more items and brand-new armors and accessories scattered throughout the world, and the content of many existing treasures has been upgraded. There are many, many new accessories that should help players craft just the right build for their team.

Expanded Prologue Tutorial
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/c90cfb739bdb174fc4f56bdc7df69297bbdd1c74.png
The Prologue is further developed with more graceful tutorials.
Solace's Tower heist section was a little under-developed, so we've expanded her adventure - along with the loot she can find. Additionally, we've taken a closer look at tutorials in the Prologue and re-worked the UI to more intuitively explain features that previously required heavy-handed tutorialization. A few tutorials will still appear so players understand the key features of Tower Song; the rest can still be found in the Guidebook in-game.

PlayStation Controller Support & More
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/a5563579f588bbb27438c132eaab750499be7fd7.png
Official support for DualShock, DualSense and Nintendo-layout controllers.
We've put in a lot of work to try and make the controller experience better, since we feel Tower Song is best enjoyed with a controller. Players now see button shortcuts on-screen (disabled in Options if desired) to help them key-in to functionality. Additionally, we have added additional button shortcuts for Equipment and Mod menus (for keyboard players too!), and players now have more options to select their controller button layout (great for controllers like 8BitDo) and shoulder buttons. Let us know if you have a controller option that we didn't account for!

More Art!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/8f41701931f890d7d03d9b0f166a5beecc4e7215.png
Many new art assets in-game, including cavern battlegrounds, Fire Tower environments, animations for Kiran and Akeno, and much more.
We're always seeking to improve, so we've added a lot more art to the game! We hope you enjoy!

Complete Patch Notes
Read on for a full list of changes made in this patch, both big and small!

New Features
New Player Character: Porphry the Fury
Play through the game as the Fury, Porphry
Players can now choose to save their game before choosing their hero, allowing them to skip the Prologue on multiple playthroughs (or just change their mind)
Players must now confirm their hero if choosing the random hero option

Exploration Abilities
Jiji can squeeze into hard to reach places to find new treasure.
Neat can talk down Song-addled victims to access forbidden areas.
Porphry can break through weak obstacles to access secret areas

Loot Revamp
There are a ton of new accessories and armors to find throughout the world.
The content of many existing chests have been upgraded; players with existing save files can backtrack to get them.
Many new chests have also been placed in the world with new items.
Players can now craft 5 full tiers of helmets and shields.

Updated Prologue & Tutorials
Solace's portion of the Tower Heist is now more involved and includes more loot to find.
Tutorials are now less intrusive and more intuitive

New Art
Additional environment art for the Fire Tower.
New battle background art in forest and desert caves
Improved animations for Kiran and Akeno's skills
And much more...

Improved Controller Support
Players can now open Equipment menu with a single button; Main Menu has been rebound to Start button
Players can now open Mod menu with a single button; Dash has been rebound to trigger/L2/R2 buttons
Button shortcuts are now persistently displayed on-screen. This can be disabled in Options.
Options: Players can now choose their button layout (great for 8Bit Do players!)
Now officially compatible with DualShock and DualSense over USB and Bluetooth. Note that Steam DS players should re-enable Steam Input to benefit from this.

Characters

Ezoan

Kido Overworld: Players can now bypass completed areas on the overworld
Vistham homes now come with windows for natural lighting. Citizens rejoice.

Foreman Yusef is no longer quite so short in cut-scenes

notes.title: Tower Song Early Access, Patch #3
notes.notes:
Greetings Tower runners; welcome to the third Early Access patch for Tower Song! This update includes some rebalancing tweaks to player-inflicted status effects, some quality of life improvements to crafting, and the usual assortment of bug fixes to make Tower Runs go that much smoother. 

As always, a big thank you to our fans and players for your diligence in finding and reporting these problems to our development team! Props to the following bug hunters this go round:
fairburrito
Tortalius
Vorticia

Want to leave us feedback for this patch or the game in general? Head on over to feedback or find us on our Discord! 

If you don't want to miss future Tower Song updates, just joining our mailing list: https://oigames.substack.com

Major Changes 

Missing Achivements
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43805649/b0c38be5426a379c553393713ef51ee402525d68.png
Fight as One and Fully Loaded can now be properly completed.
This was a big oops on our part, but we have rectified the issue. notes.notes:
Hello and welcome to Tower Song's first Early Access release! This update includes a handful of additional minor features and class tweaks, plus a true trove of bug fixes. Thanks to our fans and testers for their diligence in reporting problems to the development team!

Want to leave us feedback for this patch or the game in general? Head on over to feedback.

Now, on to the good stuff. What does Early Access Patch #1 bring us?

Major Changes
Neat's Adjustment
Adjustment now revives (and heals) dead allies when used at Stage 4-5.
This gives Neat additional benefit for holding onto his combo for longer and gives him more options to keep his team running in prolonged fights.

Crafting for Kiran and Akeno
Players can now craft lower tier weapons for Kiran and Akeno.
This allows players to better manage their loadout for late-game parties without having to choose between underpowered equipment and costly higher tier weapons.

Regen States
Regen states now provide immunity to Wounds.
It's too easy for enemies to wound regenerating allies, and regen effects are often costly to grant party members in the first place. This adjustment gives more value to classes with regen abilities.

Stun States
Removing stun effects now allies the party member to act during the round, if they haven't acted yet.
Stun is a punishing status effect to begin with and removing stun effects is not trivial. This gives increased incentive to actively remove the effect and rewards players who do so.

Boss Fight: Siege Beast
Boss' initiative greatly reduced and reinforcements now appear in stages.
The fight was nearly impossible on Hard mode, and the addition of phased reinforcements also adds additional tension to the fight. Players are now pressured to capitalize on their opportunity to damage the boss and are not punished for being unable to manage a large enemy party.

Side Quest: Missing Miners
Finding all of the miners (dead or alive) now results in a better reward.
This objective is now trackable in the quest log as well. This marks our first official side quest with many more to come!
